You are a developer-relations researcher at a company that turns SaaS apps into tools AI agents can call.
Research ONE app and fill a strict JSON schema. Use web search. Prefer the vendor's own developer docs,
API reference, pricing page, and app-review/partner pages over blogs or aggregators.

App: Podio
Category: CRM and Sales
Hint (may be misleading, verify it): podio.com

Rules
1. Every field is an object: {"value": ..., "confidence": "high|med|low", "source_url": "..."}.
2. source_url must be a page you actually saw in search results for THIS field. Never construct or guess a URL.
   If you did not find one, set value "unknown", confidence "low", source_url null.
3. "unknown" is a correct, rewarded answer. An invented answer is the worst possible answer.
4. access_path = the most restrictive step needed to use the API in production, not just to read docs.
   Self-serve OAuth client + mandatory app review for production scopes => "app_review_required".
   Free docs but the useful endpoints need a paid plan => "paid_plan_required".
5. If the thing is a command-line tool or library with no hosted API, use api_type "cli_only",
   auth_methods ["none"], access_path "not_applicable_local", toolkit_bucket "local_or_sandbox_toolkit".
6. If the hint names a different product than the app (e.g. a parent platform), research the app itself and say so in main_blocker.
7. "OAuth requested" or "coming soon" is NOT shipped. Only report auth that is documented as available.
8. official_mcp = "official" only if the vendor itself publishes or documents the MCP server.
9. confidence: high = stated explicitly on a vendor docs page; med = inferred from vendor pages; low = third-party or memory.

Allowed enums
auth_methods (array): oauth2, api_key, basic, bearer_token, jwt, hmac_signature, session_login, none, unknown
access_path: self_serve_free, self_serve_trial, paid_plan_required, app_review_required, partner_or_sales_gated, no_public_api, not_applicable_local, unknown
api_type: rest, graphql, rest_and_graphql, rpc_or_sdk_only, cli_only, none, unknown
api_breadth: broad (CRUD across many objects), narrow (a few resources), single_endpoint, none, unknown
official_mcp: official, community_only, none_found, unknown
base_url_model: fixed, per_tenant_subdomain, self_hosted_or_customer_host, regional, not_applicable, unknown
toolkit_bucket: remote_api_toolkit, local_or_sandbox_toolkit, wrap_existing_mcp, not_buildable_yet, unknown
docs_quality: full_public_reference, partial_or_thin, none_public, unknown
test_account: free_tier_or_sandbox, trial_only, none, unknown

Return ONLY this JSON, no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "one_liner": {...},        // what it does, max 15 words
  "auth_methods": {...},
  "access_path": {...},
  "api_type": {...},
  "api_breadth": {...},
  "official_mcp": {...},
  "base_url_model": {...},
  "toolkit_bucket": {...},
  "docs_quality": {...},
  "test_account": {...},
  "main_blocker": {...},     // one sentence; "none" if buildable today
  "docs_url": {...}          // primary API reference URL
}

I found the Podio API developers documentation on OAuth. Here are the key findings:

## Overview
The Podio API uses the OAuth2 protocol for authentication, which allows external apps to request authorization to Podio without having direct access to the user's password.

## Authentication Methods
The API supports different OAuth flows depending on what kind of integration you are making. Podio supports 4 ways of obtaining an access token: password (for trusted clients), authorization_code (using authorization code from the authorization flow), refresh_token (using a previously obtained refresh token), and app (logging in as an app with app ID and login token).

## Getting Started
Before you can use the Podio API you must register your application, which assigns a unique identifier called "Client ID" together with a "Client Secret," both of which are needed to authenticate.

## Recommended Approach
The recommended authentication method for the Podio API is the OAuth server-side flow. However, for automated scripts, it's recommended that you authenticate using app authentication.

The official documentation is available at https://developers.podio.com/authentication and https://developers.podio.com/doc/oauth-authorization.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Podio API rate limits, API key management, and pricing:

## Rate Limits

The general limit is 1,000 API calls per hour, but if the API call is marked as "Rate limited" in the API reference the call is deemed resource intensive and a lower rate of 250 calls per hour is enforced. Rate limits are per user per API key.

If you hit the rate limits the API will begin returning 420 HTTP error codes for all API calls. You can monitor your current status by examining two HTTP headers that are returned with each request: X-Rate-Limit-Limit: The ceiling for the request you just made and X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: The number of requests you have left for the current 1 hour window.

## API Key Requests

You have to sign in or sign up with Podio, then you find your API keys as a tab under your account settings.

## Higher Rate Limits

If you have a project that requires a higher rate limit, visit https://support.sharefile.com/s/ and contact us with a brief description of your project, your estimated usage and the client_id of the API key you are using.

## Pricing

The Podio API is free to use for both premium and free Podio accounts.

I found documentation from the Podio API for items and references. Here's what the search returned:

The Items documentation includes operations for adding new items, bulk deleting, calculating, cloning, deleting, managing references, exporting, filtering, and getting item details.

The Applications area is used to manage application definitions, which is the setup of an application consisting primarily of a list of fields and various settings.

Key item reference operations found include:

- Finding referenceable items used to find possible items for a given application field by searching relevant apps for items matching given text
- Updating item references, which tracks back the original item from which the item was cloned
- Getting item references that returns the apps and fields that reference a given item, along with the referencing items

Fields can be of different types, including "app" which holds reference links to one or more other app items.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Podio MCP server:

## Official Podio MCP Server

The Podio MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server connects AI assistants — ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Claude Desktop, and any other MCP-compatible platform — directly to your Podio data. Once connected, your AI assistant can read and write your Podio workspaces, apps, and items using plain natural language, with no coding required to get started.

The server is live at https://mcp.podio.com — just point your AI platform at it and log in with your Podio account.

The Podio MCP Server gives your AI assistant 22 tools covering both reading and writing your Podio data.

### Authentication Options

The server uses shared default credentials so you can connect immediately without creating a Podio API key, simply logging in with your Podio account when prompted. However, for production use, it's recommended to connect with your API key, and for platforms that support it (ChatGPT, Copilot Studio), creating your own Podio API key instead of relying on shared default credentials is strongly recommended.
